newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Crashed S.Korean jumbo carried 257 people-airline.
newsitem.headline: Crashed S.Korean jumbo carried 257 people-airline.

text.p: The Korean Air Lines Boeing 747 airliner that crashed in Guam on Wednesday was carrying 257 people, airline officials said.
"The Korean Air Flight 801 was carrying 234 passengers and 23 crewmembers from Seoul to Guam," airline official Cho Sung-kweon told Reuters by telephone.

Guam police said the plane crashed into a mountainside. A spokesman at Guam Memorial Hospital said reports of the number of survivors ranged from six to 29. The U.S. Navy Hospital and Guam Memorial Hospital were preparing to accept casualties.

Cho and other Korean Air Lines officials said the airliner went missing shortly before it was due to arrive early on Wednesday on the Pacific island. But the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) confirmed the crash of the plane.
"All we know is that the jumbo jet lost contact with air controllers about three miles (five km) from the airport in Guam," Cho said.
An FAA spokeswoman said the plane had just been cleared for landing at 2:35 a.m. local time on Wednesday when radar contact was lost.
